neighbours.label: 'of' inside an ordinal date phrase (the Fourth of July, the 4th of May), the slot that predicts a month name; the card's July/Jefferson focus is a stronger subcase
fire: Our cousins are flying in on the second of August to stay for a week.
The shop will be closed on the 25th of December and reopen the next day.
We signed the lease on the first of March, just before prices went up.
Her wedding is planned for the 12th of October in a small chapel.
The deadline for applications is the thirtieth of April at noon.
My grandmother was born on the 9th of February during a snowstorm.
The festival always starts on the fifteenth of August with a parade.
Rent is due on the 1st of every month, without exception.
quiet: Our cousins are flying in on August 2 to stay for a week.
The shop will be closed on December 25 and reopen the next day.
We signed the lease in early March, just before prices went up.
Her wedding is planned for October 12 in a small chapel.
The deadline for applications is April 30 at noon.
Only a fourth of the class finished the exam on time.
She came second of the twelve runners in the final race.
Rent is due at the start of each month, without exception.

predictions: ' of' after an ordinal day reaches 0.6-1.0 for any month; 'of' after ordinals in fractions or rankings ('a fourth of the cake', 'the fourth of five') and dates written without 'of' stay under 0.3.
short: 'of' in an ordinal date ('4th of July')
notes: Card: top peaks on ' of' in 'Fourth of July' / '4th of July', plus ' Jefferson', ' Declaration', ' Sp'(angled). Probe: Fourth of July 1.087, 4th of July 0.836, fourth of June 0.841, 4th of May 0.826 (not July-specific); Jefferson 0.647, Star-Spangled 0.633, Independence Day 0.595; Edison 0.040, recipe 0.012. Near misses test whether the ordinal+of or the date is the trigger.
